title: Adaptive health-tiling and shedder for region-aware autoscaler stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During cross-region failovers and sudden traffic shifts we see oscillations in autoscaler decisions driven by binary readiness/liveness signals. These oscillations cause spiky scaling (thrashing), elevated tail latency, and occasional regional degradations that violate SLOs. Goal: implement a region-aware, request-shape-sensitive health orchestration layer that produces smoothed readiness scores and an attached shedding controller to stabilize autoscaling while enabling graceful degradation under overload.
background: Recent incidents (postmortem INC-2026-07) showed two failure modes: 1) probe fanout spikes causing noisy health signals; 2) aggressive binary readiness marking that triggers autoscaler panic and cross-region failover loops. Existing mitigations (probe sampling, cooldown windows) reduced frequency but did not remove oscillation. Telemetry: sudden 30% increase in readiness-flips correlated with 18% CPU spikes and 2x autoscaler scaling events within 90s. Observed customer-visible errors: elevated 95th/99th latency and increased request error rate in failover windows.
proposal: 1) Health tiling: partition health telemetry by (region, request-shape class, backend-slot) and maintain per-tile probabilistic readiness scores (0..1) instead of binary readiness. 2) Derated readiness contract: use a sliding-window EWMA with tunable decay to smooth transient flips, and expose a 'confidence' metric for each tile. 3) Region-aware shedder: when aggregate readiness_score for a region dips below thresholds, invoke a token-aware shedder that preferentially drop or queue non-critical request classes (batchable or low-priority routing keys). 4) Autoscaler integration: feed the smoothed readiness and confidence to the autoscaler as a soft signal; add hysteresis multipliers based on region health and request-shape to reduce rapid scale-ups/downs. 5) Circuit-breaker tiers: local (node-level) fast gates, regional slower gates, and global emergency mode with configurable fallback model variants. 6) Synthetic warm lanes: proactively spin up minimal capacity for cold tiles during tail events to avoid cold-start induced readiness failures. 7) Fallback routing: coordinate with routing plane to shift traffic gradually to healthy regions based on confidence-weighted scores, using rate-limited handoff to avoid thrash.
acceptance_criteria:
- New per-tile readiness_score metric emitted for all serving nodes and visible in Grafana.
- Autoscaler accepts readiness_score as soft input and uses hysteresis multipliers.
- Under synthetic chaos test (region failure + 3x traffic), autoscaling thrash reduced by >=60% and 99th latency improved by >=25% compared to baseline.
- No customer-facing errors introduced during canary (0 known regression incidents).
- Feature controlled by runtime flags and opt-in per-customer for first wave.
tradeoffs:
- Increased complexity in probe aggregation and new metrics may add marginal CPU/ingest cost.
- Probabilistic readiness means temporary degraded answers may be served intentionally for stability, which could impact quality for some customers. We'll mitigate via per-customer opt-in and allow pinning to strict binary readiness if needed.
- Rolling this out requires tight coordination with routing and autoscaler teams to ensure contracts are respected.
milestones: 1) Design doc + API spec (done) - 2026-02-20; 2) Prototype health-tiling emitter and EWMA (in dev) - target 2026-03-05; 3) Integrate shedder and soft-autoscaler inputs (in progress) - target 2026-03-20; 4) Canary on non-critical region (staged) - target 2026-03-28; 5) Gradual rollout and postmortem review - target 2026-04-15.
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal canary in us-west on low-traffic tenants (feature flag on) for 48h with synthetic warm lanes enabled. Phase B: limited customer opt-in across 2 secondary regions with traffic shaping and observability runbook. Phase C: wider opt-in with automatic rollbacks if error budget burn > 25% in 1h. Final: global default off; enable-by-default in runtime-1.22 if metrics meet stability gates.
tests:
- Unit tests for tiling logic and EWMA computation.
- Integration tests with autoscaler simulator to validate hysteresis behavior.
- Chaos tests: node kill, region partition, sudden 3x traffic spike while running canary.
- Performance: ensure probe aggregation adds <5% CPU overhead at 95th percentile load.
- SLO validation: synthetic load tests to assert 99th latency improvement and autoscaler-thrash reduction targets in acceptance criteria.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Grafana panel 'health_tiling_summary', 'region_readiness_score', 'autoscaler_soft_signals', 'shedder_drop_rate'. Alerts: readiness_flips_rate > 10/min (P1), shedder_drop_rate > 5% sustained 10m (P2), autoscaler_thrash_count > 3 in 10m (P0). Links: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/health-tiling, https://alerts.redwood.com/alerts/health-tiling.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Meeting note: agreed on probabilistic readiness approach; PMs requested clear opt-in path for enterprise customers.
2026-02-25 - Prototype emitted per-tile metrics to dev-grafana; initial EWMA half-life tuned to 30s based on load replay.
2026-03-03 - Code review feedback from autoscaler team: prefer exposing both raw and smoothed signals; added confidence metric to proposal.
2026-03-10 - Performance run: aggregation pipeline adds ~3.6% CPU at 95th pct on test harness; acceptable per infra.
2026-03-12 - Security review: no PII in emitted tiles; KMS passthrough not required (security signoff pending automated checklist).
